brief: BTIG technical strategist Jonathan Krinsky argues the bond market just gave a 'news failure': the hot CPI print spiked the 30yr yield 8bps, but the move faded to under 2bps, which BTIG reads as confirming yields have made a tactical top. Consensus assumes lower yields are bullish for stocks, but BTIG's pain trade is the opposite: rates down, Nasdaq down. Semiconductors have already fallen alongside rates; if the Magnificent Seven follows, BTIG says that adds conviction to its 'Red October' call. The note also flags a market-structure inflection: after two-decade-low volumes, the longest SPX streak without a -1% day since 2020, and the longest NYSE 80%-downside-volume drought on record (back to 1996), today shows SPY volume ~15% above average, QQQ ~25% above average, SPX flirting with a -1% day, and 79% of NYSE volume in declining names. Separately, the SOX is down 6 straight days and SOXX 7 straight; BTIG expects a bounce soon per a 2000 analogy, but says to sell that bounce before a deeper decline.
